h1: The 6 Best Combination Small Safes of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Combination Small Safes: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six small combination safes, from battery-free mechanical dials to keypad models, with who each one suits.
summary: The Master Lock 5900D is our top pick for anyone who wants a true mechanical combination with no batteries to die. The SentrySafe Small Safe is the best compact option for a dorm or office desk. The Amazon Basics case suits buyers who need broader item coverage, and the MAESTON keypad model is for people who prefer typing a code over spinning dials.
intro: The word combination hides a real split in this category. Some small safes use a mechanical dial or wheel set that works forever with no power, while others use a keypad code that depends on batteries. Buyers who assume the two behave alike are the ones locked out after a dead battery.

We reviewed the spec sheets of small combination safes and ranked six of them. Mechanical models lead because they have one less failure point, and keypad models follow in order of the extra features they add, such as mounting hardware, alarms and multi-code access.

products.name: Master Lock Small Travel Safe with Cable, Gray Combination Lock Box, 5900D
products.verdict: A genuine battery-free combination box that travels with you.
products.description:
The Master Lock 5900D uses a true mechanical 4-digit combination, so there is nothing to charge or replace. It comes with a tether cable and a charging-cable access port, and it is listed as water-resistant. It sits in the under $25 bucket.

It takes first place because it pairs the most dependable lock type with travel-friendly touches the others skip, like the cable port. The tradeoff against the pick below is that the cable is for tethering, not for permanent mounting.

Buy it if you travel, share a hotel room or want a simple lockbox for a hostel locker. The caveat is that it is not a mountable safe, so it protects against casual theft rather than a determined thief with time.
products.idealFor: Travelers who want a simple battery-free combination box.
products.skipIf: You need a safe bolted to a wall or floor.

products.name: SentrySafe Small Safe, Black Lock Box with Combination Lock for Office or Dorm
products.verdict: A compact steel box with a no-battery three-digit lock.
products.description:
The SentrySafe Small Safe has a true mechanical 3-digit combination and solid steel construction. It measures 2.6 by 5.9 by 8.0 inches on the outside, which is sized for compact items. A tethering cable is included, and it is in the under $25 bucket.

It ranks just under the Master Lock because a 3-digit code has fewer combinations than a 4-digit one, though both avoid batteries. It beats the keypad models below on reliability.

It suits students and office workers who need to lock up a passport, spare keys or small valuables. The caveat is the small interior, so check your items against the exterior dimensions before buying.
products.idealFor: Students and office workers locking up small valuables.
products.skipIf: You need to store anything larger than a passport or phone.

products.name: Amazon Basics Portable Security Case Lock Box Safe with Combination Lock
products.verdict: A foam-lined portable case with a no-battery zinc alloy lock.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics Portable Security Case uses a true mechanical zinc alloy combination lock with no batteries. It has anti-pry steel and a foam-padded interior, and the listing states it is rated for firearms. It is in the under $25 bucket.

It sits third because the foam interior and portable case design suit a wider range of items than the tiny boxes above, but it is a case rather than a tethered or mounted safe. The Master Lock and SentrySafe offer tethering.

It is best for buyers who carry gear that needs padding. The caveat is that it is portable by design, so it can be walked away with unless you secure it elsewhere.
products.idealFor: Buyers storing padded or varied items in a portable case.
products.skipIf: You want a tether or mounting option.

products.name: MAESTON Mini Electronic Safe Box with Digital Keypad & Keys, 0.23 Cubic
products.verdict: The keypad pick with the most flexible code and mounting kit.
products.description:
The MAESTON mini safe takes a customizable 3 to 8 digit code on a battery-powered keypad. It has a magnetic auto-lock door, four pre-drilled mounting holes and two expansion bolts. It lands in the $25-50 bucket.

It leads the keypad group because it ships with mounting hardware and a longer possible code, which the other keypad boxes do not list. It trails the mechanical picks because it needs batteries.

Choose it if you want to fix a safe inside a cabinet. The caveat is the battery dependency, so keep the backup key somewhere separate.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want to bolt a keypad safe inside a cabinet.

products.name: Yuanshikj Small Steel Security Safe Box with Keypad, Key, 0.23 CuFt, Black
products.verdict: A mountable keypad box in the cheapest price bucket.
products.description:
The Yuanshikj safe is a battery-powered digital keypad model of 0.23 cubic feet. It has mountable steel construction, a magnetic auto-lock door and two emergency keys. It is in the under $25 bucket.

It ranks below the MAESTON because the listing shows no custom code range or mounting kit, but it undercuts it on price bucket. It is below the mechanical picks on reliability.

It works for buyers who are fine with a keypad and want the lowest price. The caveat is that it is not mechanical, so a dead battery means reaching for the emergency key.
products.idealFor: Keypad fans who want the lowest price.
products.skipIf: You specifically want a battery-free lock.

products.name: Voncabay Money Safe Box for Home with Digital Keypad, 0.23 Cu. Ft., Black
products.verdict: A keypad safe that warns you before the batteries die.
products.description:
The Voncabay safe has a digital keypad, an automatic interior light and a low-battery warning. It also locks out after three wrong entries for five minutes. It is a 0.23 cubic foot model in the $25-50 bucket.

Last place comes from the missing mounting kit in the listing, yet the low-battery warning and lockout address the biggest keypad weakness, surprise failure.

It suits households that want an early warning and a code-guessing lockout. The caveat is that it still relies on batteries.
products.idealFor: Households that want a warning before batteries fail.
products.skipIf: You want a mechanical, no-power lock.

whatMatters.detail: A mechanical combination uses dials or wheels and needs no power, while a keypad uses a battery-powered electronic lock. The difference matters because a dead battery can lock you out of a keypad safe. Check the listing for the phrase no batteries or battery-powered.

The number of digits sets how many combinations exist. A 3-digit code has fewer possibilities than a 4-digit one, and a keypad that accepts 3 to 8 digits gives you the longest option. Look for the exact digit range in the title or bullets.

A tether cable lets you loop a box to a fixed object, while mounting holes and expansion bolts anchor a safe in place. This matters because a portable safe can simply be carried off. Check for pre-drilled holes or a cable in the spec list.
Exterior size and usable capacity differ, so a compact box may not fit your items. A small safe holds passports and keys, not laptops. Compare the stated dimensions or cubic feet against your item.
Emergency keys and low-battery warnings give you a way in when electronics fail. Without them a keypad safe can become a problem. Check whether keys are included and where you will keep them.

howToChoose.intro: Match the lock to how much you trust batteries.

cards.label: Mechanical
cards.text: No batteries, so nothing to fail. Master Lock 5900D, SentrySafe Small Safe and Amazon Basics Portable Security Case use this.

cards.label: Keypad
cards.text: Faster to open and easier to change, but battery powered. MAESTON, Yuanshikj and Voncabay use this.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to mechanical unless they open the safe daily.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A compact body, a tether option and no battery to forget about.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The SentrySafe Small Safe is 2.6 x 5.9 x 8.0 inches with a tether cable and a mechanical lock.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want mounting hardware or a longer code, as on the MAESTON Mini Electronic Safe.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need to lock up small items, where the Master Lock 5900D already does the job.

faq.a: Mechanical ones do not. The Master Lock 5900D, SentrySafe and Amazon Basics case run without batteries, while keypad models need them.

faq.q: What happens if a keypad battery dies?
faq.a: Most listings include emergency keys, such as the Yuanshikj. Keep that key somewhere other than the safe.

faq.q: Is a keypad safe worth it over a mechanical one?
faq.a: Only if you open it often or want features like lockout and mounting. Otherwise a mechanical box is simpler.
The MAESTON includes four pre-drilled holes and two expansion bolts. The Master Lock is for tethering, not mounting.

faq.q: How do I keep a mechanical combination secret?
faq.a: Choose a code that is not a birthday and write it down away from the safe. Change it from the factory setting if the model allows.
Do not assume so. One keypad model in this group is explicitly not fireproof, so check the listing before storing documents.

finalTake: For most buyers, the Master Lock 5900D is the right call because it offers a real combination with no batteries. Dorm and office users should look at the SentrySafe for its compact size. Keypad fans get the most from the MAESTON thanks to its mounting kit. Match the lock type to your habits and the rest follows.
